title: A Voltage With Passengers
endLine: Block a door that builds voltage, and its passenger ions move less.

scenes.tts: Sodium that a blocked door missed flowed on, and cost potassium downstream. But furosemide also raises urinary calcium, and its door carries no calcium. So how?
scenes.narration: Sodium that a blocked door missed flowed on, and cost potassium downstream. But furosemide also raises urinary calcium, and its door carries no calcium. So how?
scenes.caption: Sodium that a blocked door missed flowed on, and cost potassium downstream. But furosemide also raises urinary calcium, and its door carries no calcium. So how?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 world and colour map without a reset: the long four-segment tube (proximal TEAL, thick ascending limb ORANGE, distal convoluted tubule PURPLE, collecting duct BLUE), sodium YELLOW dots, potassium MAGENTA dots, RED pumps in every cell base, WHITE charge signs, urine cup at the right end, 'schematic' tag at bottom right all film. NEW in this film: chloride CYAN dots with small minus signs; calcium and magnesium GREEN dots, drawn larger than the others and marked '2+'. During the link-back sentence, the padlocked ORANGE door from the first film glows, a YELLOW stream runs on to the blue segment, and MAGENTA dots rise into the lumen there. On 'furosemide also raises urinary calcium', GREEN dots begin to drift past the orange segment and fall into the urine cup. On the question, camera pushes in toward the ORANGE segment; large white text across the top: 'A sodium door moves calcium?'

Title 'A Voltage With Passengers' fades in for 2 s while the question text fades out. The padlock lifts off the ORANGE door (reset to an unblocked thick limb). The camera completes its push-in: one ORANGE-walled thick-limb cell fills about 65% of frame height, with a neighbour cell at each edge and a narrow gap (junction) between them; lumen above, body side below, RED pump turning in the base. This close-up is the world for the rest of the film until s13.

scenes.tts: In nineteen seventy-three, Rocha and Kokko held single rabbit thick limbs on glass pipettes. Salt left the fluid, but water stayed. And the lumen sat positive, about seven millivolts.
scenes.narration: In 1973, Rocha and Kokko held single rabbit thick limbs on glass pipettes. Salt left the fluid, but water stayed. And the lumen sat positive, about 7 mV.
scenes.caption: In 1973, Rocha and Kokko held single rabbit thick limbs on glass pipettes. Salt left the fluid, but water stayed. And the lumen sat positive, about 7 mV.
scenes.visual: Two simple glass pipette cartoons slide in from the left and right edges and hold the ends of the lumen, labelled 'isolated rabbit tubule'. On 'Salt left', YELLOW and CYAN dots leave the lumen down through the cell; on 'water stayed', a few pale water drops in the lumen stay put and bounce off the walls, labelled 'water stays'. On 'positive', WHITE plus signs appear in the lumen, and a vertical voltage gauge appears at the right edge, scale 0 to +10 mV, labelled 'lumen voltage'; its needle rises to +7 with the label 'about +7 mV'. The gauge stays for the rest of the film.

scenes.tts: Its door, N K C C two, carries one sodium, one potassium and two chlorides together. That is no net charge. So where does the voltage come from?
scenes.narration: Its door, NKCC2, carries one sodium, one potassium and two chlorides together. That is no net charge. So where does the voltage come from?
scenes.caption: Its door, NKCC2, carries one sodium, one potassium and two chlorides together. That is no net charge. So where does the voltage come from?
scenes.visual: The pipettes fade. The ORANGE door in the top membrane, labelled 'NKCC2', turns one notch: exactly one YELLOW, one MAGENTA and two CYAN dots pass in together. A small tally beside the door counts '+1 +1 −2 = 0'. It repeats every 2 s for the rest of the film whenever the door is unblocked. The voltage gauge holds at +7 with a question mark beside it.

scenes.tts: Follow each ion out. Sodium leaves toward the blood through the pump. Chloride leaves toward the blood through chloride channels. Negative charge has crossed to the blood side.
scenes.narration: Follow each ion out. Sodium leaves toward the blood through the pump. Chloride leaves toward the blood through chloride channels. Negative charge has crossed to the blood side.
scenes.caption: Follow each ion out. Sodium leaves toward the blood through the pump. Chloride leaves toward the blood through chloride channels. Negative charge has crossed to the blood side.
scenes.visual: YELLOW dots inside the cell leave through the RED pump in the base. A CYAN channel opens in the basolateral membrane, labelled 'Cl− channel'; CYAN dots leave through it into the body side, which is now labelled 'blood side'. On 'Negative charge', WHITE minus signs collect in the blood side below the cell. MAGENTA dots stay inside the cell, waiting.

scenes.tts: Now potassium. Tubular fluid holds little of it, compared with sodium and chloride. So how does this door keep getting the potassium it needs?
scenes.narration: Now potassium. Tubular fluid holds little of it, compared with sodium and chloride. So how does this door keep getting the potassium it needs?
scenes.caption: Now potassium. Tubular fluid holds little of it, compared with sodium and chloride. So how does this door keep getting the potassium it needs?
scenes.visual: In the lumen, YELLOW and CYAN dots are many and MAGENTA dots very few. The NKCC2 door slows as it waits for a MAGENTA dot. Question card across the top in white: 'Where does its potassium come from?'

Predict pause. The question card stays. Near-stillness by design: the NKCC2 door holds mid-turn, MAGENTA dots inside the cell bob in place, the gauge needle trembles near +7, the RED pump turns slowly.

scenes.tts: It recycles. Most of the potassium goes back into the lumen, through the potassium channel R O M K. Positive charge returns to the lumen side.
scenes.narration: It recycles. Most of the potassium goes back into the lumen, through the potassium channel ROMK. Positive charge returns to the lumen side.
scenes.caption: It recycles. Most of the potassium goes back into the lumen, through the potassium channel ROMK. Positive charge returns to the lumen side.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves. A MAGENTA channel opens in the top membrane beside the NKCC2 door, labelled 'ROMK'. MAGENTA dots leave the cell through it into the lumen and are picked up again by the NKCC2 door: a visible MAGENTA loop, door in, ROMK out. On 'Positive charge', WHITE plus signs gather in the lumen above the ROMK channel. The NKCC2 door returns to its steady 2 s rhythm.

scenes.tts: Negative charge goes to the blood, and positive charge goes back to the lumen. So the lumen ends up a few millivolts positive. The circuit around the door makes the voltage.
scenes.narration: Negative charge goes to the blood, and positive charge goes back to the lumen. So the lumen ends up a few millivolts positive. The circuit around the door makes the voltage.
scenes.caption: Negative charge goes to the blood, and positive charge goes back to the lumen. So the lumen ends up a few millivolts positive. The circuit around the door makes the voltage.
scenes.visual: The CYAN exit path and the MAGENTA loop glow together as one circuit outlined around the door, labelled 'circuit'. WHITE minus signs sit below the cell, WHITE plus signs above it. The gauge's question mark disappears; the needle holds at +7. Small tag beside the cell: 'classic one-cell picture'.

scenes.tts: The junctions between these cells let cations through. The positive lumen pushes them out between the cells, toward the blood. Calcium and magnesium carry two charges each, so they are pushed twice as hard.
scenes.narration: The junctions between these cells let cations through. The positive lumen pushes them out between the cells, toward the blood. Calcium and magnesium carry two charges each, so they are pushed twice as hard.
scenes.caption: The junctions between these cells let cations through. The positive lumen pushes them out between the cells, toward the blood. Calcium and magnesium carry two charges each, so they are pushed twice as hard.
scenes.visual: Camera slides a little to the gap between the cell and its right neighbour; the junction near the top glows, labelled 'cation-selective junction'. A few YELLOW dots and GREEN '2+' dots in the lumen slip down through the gap into the blood side, nudged by the WHITE plus signs. On 'two charges', each GREEN dot gets a double arrow pointing down, each YELLOW dot a single arrow. The GREEN dots move through the gap faster than the YELLOW ones.

scenes.tts: How low can plus seven millivolts push them? At body temperature, lumen over blood equals e to the minus charge times voltage over twenty-six point seven millivolts. Put in plus seven millivolts. For one charge, the lumen can fall as low as seventy-seven percent of its blood level. For two charges, as low as fifty-nine percent. That is an equilibrium limit, not a measurement.
scenes.narration: How low can plus seven millivolts push them? At body temperature, lumen over blood equals e to the minus charge times voltage over twenty-six point seven millivolts. Put in plus seven millivolts. For one charge, the lumen can fall as low as seventy-seven percent of its blood level. For two charges, as low as fifty-nine percent. That is an equilibrium limit, not a measurement.
scenes.caption: How low can plus seven millivolts push them? At body temperature, lumen over blood equals e to the minus charge times voltage over twenty-six point seven millivolts. Put in plus seven millivolts. For one charge, the lumen can fall as low as seventy-seven percent of its blood level. For two charges, as low as fifty-nine percent. That is an equilibrium limit, not a measurement.
scenes.visual: Beside the gap, two vertical bars, each with a full-height outline labelled 'blood level'. Bar 1, YELLOW, labelled 'one charge', fills to 0.77 of the outline; bar 2, GREEN, labelled 'two charges', fills to 0.59. Values computed as exp(−zV/26.7 mV) at V = +7 mV, the lesson's equilibrium limit. Tag under both bars: 'equilibrium limit, not measured'. GREEN dots keep slipping through the gap. Label the bars as lumen level relative to blood level. Write the formula exp(−z × 7 mV / 26.7 mV) beside the bars as spoken, showing z = 1 → 0.77 (77%) and z = 2 → 0.59 (59%), with a downward arrow inside each outline showing the lumen level falling toward its bar.

scenes.tts: That is why this segment matters for magnesium most of all. Textbook estimates credit it with about sixty to seventy percent of filtered magnesium. For calcium, the estimate is about twenty to twenty-five percent.
scenes.narration: That is why this segment matters for magnesium most of all. Textbook estimates credit it with about 60–70% of filtered magnesium. For calcium, the estimate is about 20–25%.
scenes.caption: That is why this segment matters for magnesium most of all. Textbook estimates credit it with about 60–70% of filtered magnesium. For calcium, the estimate is about 20–25%.
scenes.visual: The two bars fade. At the bottom of the frame, two short horizontal range bars in GREEN appear, each on a 0 to 100% scale: 'magnesium: 60–70%' shaded from 60 to 70, and 'calcium: 20–25%' shaded from 20 to 25. Tag: 'textbook estimates'. GREEN dots continue to cross the junction.

scenes.tts: Here is the one idea. A door can move ions it never carries, if its segment builds a voltage. Block that door, and the voltage's passengers move much less.
scenes.narration: Here is the one idea. A door can move ions it never carries, if its segment builds a voltage. Block that door, and the voltage's passengers move much less.
scenes.caption: Here is the one idea. A door can move ions it never carries, if its segment builds a voltage. Block that door, and the voltage's passengers move much less.
scenes.visual: The range bars fade. The full circuit glows around the NKCC2 door while GREEN dots cross the junction; label 'passengers' over the GREEN dots. On 'Block that door', the padlock from the first film closes on the ORANGE door again, labelled 'furosemide'. No dots enter. The MAGENTA loop and CYAN exit fade, the WHITE plus signs in the lumen thin out, and the gauge needle falls well below +7 (schematic, no number). Most GREEN dots stop at the junction and drift on along the lumen; only a few still cross.

scenes.tts: That is how furosemide, blocking a sodium door, ends up raising urinary calcium. The proximal tubule also takes back calcium between its cells, more than the thick limb does. This rule leaves that out.
scenes.narration: That is how furosemide, blocking a sodium door, ends up raising urinary calcium. The proximal tubule also takes back calcium between its cells, more than the thick limb does. This rule leaves that out.
scenes.caption: That is how furosemide, blocking a sodium door, ends up raising urinary calcium. The proximal tubule also takes back calcium between its cells, more than the thick limb does. This rule leaves that out.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the first film's whole tube. GREEN dots that passed the padlocked ORANGE segment flow on to the right and fall into the urine cup, which gains a GREEN layer. On 'The proximal tubule', the TEAL segment glows and GREEN dots cross between its cells into the body side, with a small label 'not in this rule'. The orange segment's lost voltage is shown by its WHITE plus signs gone.

scenes.tts: So look past what a door carries. Ask what voltage its segment was building, and which ions that voltage moved.
scenes.narration: So look past what a door carries. Ask what voltage its segment was building, and which ions that voltage moved.
scenes.caption: So look past what a door carries. Ask what voltage its segment was building, and which ions that voltage moved.
scenes.visual: Slow push back toward the ORANGE segment. The padlock lifts; the NKCC2 door turns, the MAGENTA loop and CYAN exit restart, WHITE plus signs return to the lumen and GREEN dots resume crossing between the cells. The gauge rises back to +7.

End card over the dimmed but still moving thick-limb cell, large white text, centred: 'Block a door that builds voltage, and its passenger ions move less.' GREEN dots drift slowly through the junction behind it; the MAGENTA loop keeps turning.
